evaluation.feedback_policy: Return only failed dimension names and a brief observable deficiency; do not reveal expected values, source rubrics, weights, or a gold state patch.

source_rubrics: The response should provide counts of wins by color (White vs Black) derived from the response’s own wins table (i.e., the number of “White” rows and “Black” rows in the wins table should match the stated counts).
The response should report the time-control (time restraint) counts for wins as: 10+0 = 14, 15+5 = 1, 15+10 = 1, 15+0 = 1, 25+0 = 1, 3+0 = 1, and “no control specified” = 1
The response should report the ECO counts among wins as: D00 = 6, A40 = 4, B00 = 4, D02 = 3, A45 = 1, A00 = 1, C44 = 1
The response should compute Elo difference for each win as ([my Elo] − [opponent Elo]) and present it as a signed integer (negative/zero/positive)
The response should list the Elo difference for the win at 23/02/2026@05:21:48 (I played Black; WhiteElo 1372 vs BlackElo 1028) as −344
The response should list the Elo difference for the win at 16/02/2026@22:39:06 (I played White; WhiteElo 1028 vs BlackElo 712) as +316
The response should include a wins table containing exactly 20 rows (one per win) sorted by Date/Time ascending from 28/01/2026@18:06:34 through 24/02/2026@04:39:29
The response should include, for each row in the wins table, all of the following fields: Date/Time, Color (White/Black), Termination, TimeControl, ECO, Elo Diff, and Event
The response should label the termination for these five wins as “Time forfeit”: 29/01/2026@15:41:16, 29/01/2026@17:18:45, 03/02/2026@06:07:44, 13/02/2026@01:55:11, and 13/02/2026@19:11:50
The response should not contain internal contradictions where a summary count (e.g., “Time forfeit wins = 1”) disagrees with the number of matching entries in the response’s own wins table
The response should identify the declared win streak cluster as exactly 7 consecutive wins occurring between 21/02/2026 and 24/02/2026

The response should identify at least one additional win cluster outside the declared streak and specify its start and end Date/Time. (“Cluster” here means 2 or more consecutive wins with no losses/draws between them in chronological order.)

The response should identify at least one loss cluster and specify its start and end Date/Time. (“Loss cluster” here means 2 or more consecutive losses with no wins/draws between them in chronological order.)
The response should include the duration for each cluster it identifies, expressed as elapsed time between the first and last game timestamps (e.g., in hours/days)
The response should compute inter-game intervals (time gaps) between consecutive games using the provided timestamps and use those computed gaps in the correlation discussion
The response should compare at least two interval summaries (e.g., average/median gap or distribution buckets) between (a) the 7-win streak cluster and (b) a non-streak period

The response should support any claimed relationship between breaks and performance with at least one concrete, computed example (e.g., “there was a ~X-hour/day gap before cluster Y, and the next Z games were wins/losses”)
